challenges.name: test-matrix-quiz
challenges.title: Read the matrix runs
challenges.description: Three statements about the first runs of Rice Rocket's integration test matrix. Decide whether each one is true.
hints: Expand the matrix by hand: write every node/os pair, then apply the `include` entry with GitHub's rule about not overwriting an original matrix value.
Read the last line of the run log: which setting decided that one failure stops the other combinations, and what is its default?
Where does the test process run: on the runner's virtual machine, or inside a container on the job's Docker network? Which of the two can resolve the name `postgres`?

questions.question:
The team wants coverage from one combination only:

```yaml
strategy:
  matrix:
    node: [22, 24]
    os: [ubuntu-24.04, windows-2025]
    include:
      - node: 24
        os: ubuntu-24.04
        coverage: true
```

Statement: "This matrix starts 5 jobs: the four node/os combinations, plus one extra job on Node 24 and Ubuntu that collects coverage."
questions.explanation: False. It starts 4 jobs. An `include` entry is added to every original combination it can join without overwriting an original matrix value; `{node: 24, os: ubuntu-24.04}` already exists, so that job just gains `coverage: true` (read as `matrix.coverage`, empty in the other three). An include entry creates a new combination only when it would overwrite an original value, as `node: 25` would. The misconception is that every `include` entry adds a job.

questions.question:
The first matrix run after a pull request that changed a query:

```text
integration (22, 16)   failed after 1m 12s
integration (22, 17)   cancelled
integration (24, 16)   cancelled
integration (24, 17)   cancelled

The strategy configuration was canceled because "integration._22_16" failed
```

Statement: "With `fail-fast: false` in the strategy, the three other combinations would run to the end, and their results would show whether the failure is specific to Postgres 16, to Node 22, or to neither."
questions.explanation: True. `fail-fast` defaults to `true`: the first failing job of a matrix cancels every job of that matrix that is still queued or running. Here that hid the only useful information. With `fail-fast: false` every combination reports its own result; if (22, 17) and (24, 17) pass while (24, 16) fails too, the query depends on a Postgres 17 feature. The cost is paying for the runs that continue after a failure.

questions.question:
The job runs on the runner, with Postgres as a service container; the URL was copied from `compose.yaml`:

```yaml
jobs:
  integration:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    services:
      postgres:
        image: postgres:17
        ports:
          - 5432:5432
    steps:
      - run: npm run test:integration
        env:
          DATABASE_URL: postgres://postgres:test@postgres:5432/postgres
```

```text
Error: getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND postgres
```

Statement: "The service name resolves only when the job itself runs in a container (`container:`); a job running directly on the runner reaches the service through the mapped port on `localhost`."
questions.explanation: True. Service containers join a Docker network that the job's own container is attached to when the job uses `container:`; there, `postgres` resolves through Docker's DNS. A job without `container:` runs on the runner VM, outside that network, and reaches the service only through the port published on the host: `localhost:5432` with `ports: - 5432:5432`. The misconception is that Actions services work like Compose services for every job.

challenges.name: node-postgres-test-matrix
challenges.title: Test every Node and Postgres version, all the way through
challenges.description: The api has to pass on Node 22 and 24 and on Postgres 16 (staging) and 17 (production). The first matrix run was useless: one failure cancelled the other combinations, the tests looked for the database at the host `postgres` and got `ENOTFOUND`, and the runs that did connect flaked with `the database system is starting up`. The editor holds the integration workflow with its matrix, service and test settings missing, each marked by a `# [ ]` line; some pieces are wrong on purpose. Fill every line so that: the job runs once per Node 22/24 x Postgres 16/17 combination, plus one experimental combination of Node 25 with Postgres 17; each combination starts a Postgres service of its own matrix version and waits until it accepts connections; the tests reach it from the runner; a failing combination never cancels the others; and a failure of the experimental combination does not fail the run, while any other failure does. Run grades the file with a simulator of the matrix, the service container network and fail-fast.
hints: Take each symptom in turn: what cancelled the other combinations, which network the test process is on when it resolves the database host, and who waits for Postgres before `npm run test:integration` starts.

Look at `strategy.fail-fast`, `strategy.matrix` with `include`, `jobs.<id>.continue-on-error` with a matrix expression, and a service container's `image`, `ports` and `options` (the `--health-*` flags).

A Redis-backed job on the runner tested on two Redis versions: `matrix: { redis: [7, 8] }`, `services: { redis: { image: "redis:${{ matrix.redis }}", ports: ["6379:6379"], options: "--health-cmd 'redis-cli ping' --health-interval 5s" } }`, and `REDIS_URL: redis://localhost:6379` on the test step.

tests.name: Four Node x Postgres combinations plus the experimental Node 25 one
Each combination gets its own Postgres version, reachable and ready
A Postgres 16 bug on Node 22 fails the run and cancels nothing
A failure on the experimental Node 25 combination does not fail the run
A bug on both Postgres 16 combinations shows on both, the run fails
